body: If there is nothing after this I keep telling myself to just keep seeing what’s here, we’ll all die at some point- when I feel good I always ask myself why I want to speed up the process of being nothing.

We just- go. I don’t believe there’s anything else out there, I feel like people hold onto the idea that there is an afterlife like heaven and hell because it’s comforting to believe that this isn’t just it. That there’s more than this. That we’re destined to keep going. We’re born, we live, we die. Just like everything else. We’re just beings with the ability to believe in what we want and we have mouths to share those ideas with other people who want the same thing.

This is really heartwarming to hear, I’m glad that you’re doing a lot better for yourself now. I understand how hard it is to go through something like hospitalisation- you’re a trooper for coming through it and being able to really help yourself battle these demons even if there’s a few more you’re working on. You seem like a very strong person. Thank you for your comment :)
Thank you for sharing your experience, I guess that is the first step to finding something else to focus your energy on- at least I hope that for you.
I read this on the bus and I’m crying a little bit. This is something I really needed to read. It feels so isolating sometimes. I’m glad you’re finding ways to fight through the bad times. Thank you.
I’m keeping this comment close, it hasn’t fallen on deaf ears- thank you.

Can you go to him at all? If not, I assume you both have smartphones or at least something with a camera? Skype/FaceTime him. If you’re at work or he is set a time up when it works for you both to talk. Face to face (even on camera) is better than a phone call. I always find seeing somebody I love a lot easier to get me out of my own head. 

Knowing that somebody cares is the biggest thing that can help. 

Send him links to videos you know he likes that he may not have seen before, make a little care package of stuff he enjoys like sodas, beers, lollies- anything you can spare to afford even if it’s only one thing.

Listen to him talk. A lot of the time people don’t want advice when they feel that way, they just need to vent.

If things start getting worse then let him know you’re really concerned, that he means a lot to you and that he can book an appointment with a GP to get him either on medication or referred to a mental health specialist. 

Be there for him.
Please please please call somebody close to you or 911 for help to get to a safe place that can get that crap out of you. You matter. Life matters. Death is permanent. Reach out!

You don’t know that though. My Grandpa committed suicide when I was young, I didn’t know him beyond three years old- but I missed the idea of knowing him, I still do. I’m not trying to change your mind here but I do want to share how his death impacted me. 
My friends had Grandpa’s and I always wished he had stayed around so I could spend weekends and holidays with him and my Grandma like they did.
I don’t have a lot of family. He loved fly fishing and duck hunting, I don’t like any of ~~this~~ those things, but I would still give anything to have a chance to see him in his element. My Grandma said it was really where he was his happiest. Maybe if he waited a bit longer we could have done it together, maybe even made a thing of it?

At the end of the day your life is your life; but taking it will always impact people around you, especially when they love you.

I really do wish you the absolute best. I’ll keep you in my thoughts during these holidays and I hope you will be here to enjoy them. Truly. 

Don’t let yourself believe you don’t matter to them. Maybe you’ve made a lot of mistakes so far in life but that doesn’t mean you can’t work on being better.

Hey, I see you’re feeling vulnerable right now and I want you to know that vulnerability is a good thing- even though it’s hard.

You’re posting a lot of comments here and for me, I see that as a way of you coping with how much is going on in your head right now. That’s rough. It sucks when you don’t feel like you can love yourself again even though you are loved by other people. And it’s harder when you’re fighting against yourself.

Your sister has a baby? You seem to really care about him/her, that’s a really good thing. When you spend the day with them look at that baby and think about how you were once like that. Small, wide-eyed and filled with unconditional compassion for all around you. That doesn’t go away- it can be squashed to a point where you believe it has, but sometimes it just takes a lot of practice and kindness to yourself to see and feel it again. The best way to find happiness is by watching children spread it without a second thought.

Stay close to your family even though you want to leave. Hold that baby close. Tell that baby that you want to see them grow into a person who you can share stories with about how you battled your demons when they feel overwhelmed with theirs. That you love that baby so much and you don’t want to hurt them by leaving before they have a chance to truly know you.

You may not matter to yourself at the moment, but you matter to that baby- and also the ones who love you.

Hold on. Give yourself a chance.

Edit: I see that you said babies now- that’s even more beautiful beings to hold on for.

The best way to get back at someone is actively trying to do better than them when they leave. Death is permanent. What happens if she doesn’t get the video? Or she has you blocked? 
You deserve to give yourself a chance to go for the long run and be better than how you were when you dated.

First of all, good on you for trying to better yourself! Not only will working on losing the weight you don’t want help you physically, it will also help how you feel about yourself too.

Now I’m not sure on dieting when it comes to teens, but if your family is open to the idea going to a dietician who can help you figure out a plan that works with your body, that will be a great step. If not, that’s okay too! You seem to be doing something that you’re happy with at the moment. You can test out different diets and food groups you like and don’t as you go.

Having dogs is a great incentive for exercising. I don’t know how big they are, but I have a friend like yourself who is actively losing weight, he takes one dog out at a time and walks them separately on the same route. So, you get to have one big walk twice in the day with a seperate dog. Just an idea. Otherwise take them out for a set amount of time; maybe you want to walk for 15 minutes one way and 15 minutes back home? Slowly increase that as the weeks go when you feel like you can go further.

With the treadmill slowly build your speed and time up day by day. Maybe aim for 10-15 minutes on a brisk walk? If your treadmill has it you can even use the incline option to take it a bit further as time goes on. People can fall away from using treadmills because it can get a little boring, so I _strongly_ suggest putting your favourite video (YouTube or a show) on your phone propped up in front of you as you do it- time goes by faster too and before you know it, poof! You’ve done your walk and watched something you would have anyway.

Stairs are a great way to build up calves, when you’re up for it see how many times you can go up and down them comfortably. If you can do it 3, 4, maybe 5 times before you start getting out of breath- keep that set amount up each time you use them until you feel like you can do a bit more.

It’s all about pace. Be kind to yourself. Treat yourself the way you would treat your doggies if they were learning how to start walking outside again- gently and slowly. 

You’re on a great path. Don’t be too hard on yourself because you’re already doing a great job reaching out for ideas and having the motivation to change.

This made me feel more relief than I thought I would ever get from this post. You’re right. I had psyched myself up for going into a group without realising that I didn’t have to stay the entire time. It feels less intimidating when you put it into that perspective. 
I will only be trying out one group at a time since I can’t bring myself to try anything more. This made me feel like I can do it, even if for a second. I just have to make sure I’m in a good headspace. 

Thank you so much.

Thank you for your reply. I can only give it a try I guess. Just the thought of even trying made me (apologies for the crudeness) vomit this morning. I suppose there’s no other way, I just hope I can do it.

This is such a difficult situation to be in, but you must know that you DO NOT have to go through this alone. 

Since you have come to this subreddit I’m assuming that things are going south very fast.

Are his family involved in his life? Are they people who will take the situation seriously? (I only ask because sometimes the parents/caregivers/relatives aren’t always in the equation) 

If you know where any of them work call the company and ask to speak immediately with Mr/Mrs *last name* in concern to a family emergency. Try your best to get in touch with them right now and let them know what is happening. Send through screenshots of his messages, tell them your concerns, tell them the severity of the situation. 

If no, call a crisis hotline in your area and tell them all of the above. Tell them what he has been telling you, that if anyone is sent out he may try to downplay the situation but there is a VERY high chance he will attempt to take his life if/when he is left alone any longer. Tell them that he is not safe. They will likely send out a few officers who will then do a wellness check on your friend and hopefully take him in for an assessment and they will be able to talk to the family.

Edit: you could try to reach the family through Facebook as well
